sanskrit: iti śrutvā ca tattvena bhīṣmaḥ kurupitāmahaḥ tato gāndhārarājasya preṣayām āsa bhārata
english: Having truly heard this, Bhīṣma, the grandsire of the Kurus, thereupon dispatched a messenger to the king of Gāndhāra, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: acakṣur iti tatrāsīt subalasya vicāraṇā kulaṃ khyātiṃ ca vṛttaṃ ca buddhyā tu prasamīkṣya saḥ dadau tāṃ dhṛtarāṣṭrāya gāndhārīṃ dharmacāriṇīm
english: There was hesitation on the part of Subala on account of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's blindness; but weighing carefully with his intellect the family, the fame, and the conduct of the Kurus, he gave Gāndhārī, that virtuous woman, to Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: gāndhārī tv api śuśrāva dhṛtarāṣṭram acakṣuṣam ātmānaṃ ditsitaṃ cāsmai pitrā mātrā ca bhārata
english: Gāndhārī too had heard that Dhṛtarāṣṭra was blind and that she was being given to him by her father and mother, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tataḥ sā paṭṭam ādāya kṛtvā bahuguṇaṃ śubhā babandha netre sve rājan pativrataparāyaṇā nātyaśnīyāṃ patim aham ity evaṃ kṛtaniścayā
english: Then that auspicious woman, devoted to her vow of fidelity to her husband, resolved that she would not surpass her lord; she took a strip of cloth, folded it many times, and bound it over her own eyes, O king.

sanskrit: tato gāndhārarājasya putraḥ śakunir abhyayāt svasāraṃ parayā lakṣmyā yuktām ādāya kauravān
english: Then Śakuni, son of the king of Gāndhāra, came bringing his sister, endowed with great beauty, to the Kauravas.

sanskrit: dattvā sa bhaginīṃ vīro yathārhaṃ ca paricchadam punar āyāt svanagaraṃ bhīṣmeṇa pratipūjitaḥ
english: That hero, having given his sister along with fitting gifts and apparel, returned to his own city, having been honored by Bhīṣma.

sanskrit: gāndhāry api varārohā śīlācāraviceṣṭitaiḥ tuṣṭiṃ kurūṇāṃ sarveṣāṃ janayām āsa bhārata
english: Gāndhārī too, that most excellent woman, through her conduct, deportment, and behavior, gave satisfaction to all the Kurus, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: vṛttenārādhya tān sarvān pativrataparāyaṇā vācāpi puruṣān anyān suvratā nānvakīrtayat
english: Devoted to her vow of chastity, she propitiated them all by her conduct; and firm in her vow, she never praised even in speech any other man.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca śūro nāma yaduśreṣṭho vasudevapitābhavat tasya kanyā pṛthā nāma rūpeṇāsadṛśī bhuvi
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: There was a foremost of the Yadus named Śūra who was the father of Vāsudeva; he had a daughter named Pṛthā, unequaled in beauty on earth.

sanskrit: paitṛṣvaseyāya sa tām anapatyāya vīryavān agryam agre pratijñāya svasyāpatyasya vīryavān
english: That mighty hero, having first made a solemn promise to his father's sister's son who was childless, gave to him the first-born of his own offspring.

sanskrit: agrajāteti tāṃ kanyām agryānugrahakāṅkṣiṇe pradadau kuntibhojāya sakhā sakhye mahātmane
english: He gave that first-born daughter, whom he had pledged as the foremost gift, to Kuntibhoja, his great-souled friend — given friend to friend.

sanskrit: sā niyuktā pitur gehe devatātithipūjane ugraṃ paryacarad ghoraṃ brāhmaṇaṃ saṃśitavratam
english: She, appointed in her father's house to the service of gods and guests, attended with devotion a fierce and terrible Brahmin of intense austerity.

sanskrit: nigūḍhaniścayaṃ dharme yaṃ taṃ durvāsasaṃ viduḥ tam ugraṃ saṃśitātmānaṃ sarvayatnair atoṣayat
english: Him of deep resolve in righteousness, whom they know as Durvasa — that fierce one of sharpened spirit — she pleased by every effort.

sanskrit: tasyai sa pradadau mantram āpaddharmānvavekṣayā abhicārābhisaṃyuktam abravīc caiva tāṃ muniḥ
english: Considering the dharma applicable in times of difficulty, he gave her a mantra endowed with power to summon, and the sage spoke thus to her.

sanskrit: yaṃ yaṃ devaṃ tvam etena mantreṇāvāhayiṣyasi tasya tasya prasādena putras tava bhaviṣyati
english: Whichever deity you invoke with this mantra, by that deity's favor a son shall be born to you.

sanskrit: tathoktā sā tu vipreṇa tena kautūhalāt tadā kanyā satī devam arkam ājuhāva yaśasvinī
english: Thus addressed by that Brahmin, that virtuous and glorious maiden, out of curiosity, then invoked the sun-god Arka.

sanskrit: sā dadarśa tam āyāntaṃ bhāskaraṃ lokabhāvanam vismitā cānavadyāṅgī dṛṣṭvā tan mahad adbhutam
english: She saw the sun, the illuminator of worlds, coming toward her; that woman of flawless limbs was filled with wonder upon beholding that great marvel.

sanskrit: prakāśakarmā tapanas tasyāṃ garbhaṃ dadhau tataḥ ajījanat tato vīraṃ sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varam āmuktakavacaḥ śrīmān devagarbhaḥ śriyāvṛtaḥ
english: Then the sun, whose work is to shine, placed his seed in her; she thereupon gave birth to a hero, the foremost of all who bear weapons — born already wearing his armor, splendid, divine in origin, and invested with radiance.

sanskrit: sahajaṃ kavacaṃ bibhrat kuṇḍaloddyotitānanaḥ ajāyata sutaḥ karṇaḥ sarvalokeṣu viśrutaḥ
english: Bearing his natural armor and with his face lit by his earrings, was born the son Karṇa, renowned in all the worlds.

sanskrit: prādāc ca tasyāḥ kanyātvaṃ punaḥ sa paramadyutiḥ dattvā ca dadatāṃ śreṣṭho divam ācakrame tataḥ
english: That most resplendent one, best among givers, restored her maidenhood to her, and having given thus, ascended to heaven.

sanskrit: gūhamānāpacāraṃ taṃ bandhupakṣabhayāt tadā utsasarja jale kuntī taṃ kumāraṃ salakṣaṇam
english: Concealing that transgression out of fear of her kinsmen, Kuntī then cast that auspiciously marked infant into the water.

sanskrit: tam utsṛṣṭaṃ tadā garbhaṃ rādhābhartā mahāyaśāḥ putratve kalpayām āsa sabhāryaḥ sūtanandanaḥ
english: That abandoned child was then adopted as a son by the greatly renowned husband of Rādhā, a son of a suta, together with his wife.

sanskrit: nāmadheyaṃ ca cakrāte tasya bālasya tāv ubhau vasunā saha jāto 'yaṃ vasuṣeṇo bhavatv iti
english: Those two gave a name to that infant: "Since he was born along with wealth, let him be called Vasushena."

sanskrit: sa vardhamāno balavān sarvāstreṣūdyato 'bhavat ā pṛṣṭhatāpād ādityam upatasthe sa vīryavān
english: Growing up and becoming powerful, he applied himself to all weapons; that mighty hero would stand in worship of the sun until the heat touched his back.

sanskrit: yasmin kāle japann āste sa vīraḥ satyasaṃgaraḥ nādeyaṃ brāhmaṇeṣv āsīt tasmin kāle mahātmanaḥ
english: At the time when that hero of truthful pledge sat muttering prayers, there was nothing that this great-souled one would refuse to give to Brahmins.

sanskrit: tam indro brāhmaṇo bhūtvā bhikṣārthaṃ bhūtabhāvanaḥ kuṇḍale prārthayām āsa kavacaṃ ca mahādyutiḥ
english: Indra, the nourisher of all beings and of great splendor, taking the form of a Brahmin, approached him as a suppliant and begged for his earrings and his armor.

sanskrit: utkṛtya vimanāḥ svāṅgāt kavacaṃ rudhirasravam karṇas tu kuṇḍale chittvā prāyacchat sa kṛtāñjaliḥ
english: Karṇa, though pained, cut off from his own body his armor dripping with blood, and severing his earrings, gave them with joined palms.

sanskrit: śaktiṃ tasmai dadau śakraḥ vismito vākyam abravīt devāsuramanuṣyāṇāṃ gandharvoragarakṣasām yasmai kṣepsyasi ruṣṭaḥ san so 'nayā na bhaviṣyati
english: Śakra, astonished, gave him the Shakti weapon and said: "Among gods, asuras, men, gandharvas, serpents, and rakshasas — at whomever you hurl this in anger, he shall be no more."

sanskrit: purā nāma tu tasyāsīd vasuṣeṇa iti śrutam tato vaikartanaḥ karṇaḥ karmaṇā tena so 'bhavat
english: His former name had been known as Vasushena; thereafter by that deed he became Vaikartana Karṇa — the cutter of his own flesh.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca rūpasattvaguṇopetā dharmārāmā mahāvratā duhitā kuntibhojasya kṛte pitrā svayaṃvare
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: The daughter of Kuntibhoja, endowed with beauty, valor, and virtue, devoted to righteousness and of great vows, was presented by her father at a swayamvara.

sanskrit: siṃhadaṃṣṭraṃ gajaskandham ṛṣabhākṣaṃ mahābalam bhūmipālasahasrāṇāṃ madhye pāṇḍum avindata
english: She chose Pāṇḍu — lion-fanged, elephant-shouldered, bull-eyed, and of great might — from among thousands of kings.

sanskrit: sa tayā kuntibhojasya duhitrā kurunandanaḥ yuyuje 'mitasaubhāgyaḥ paulomyā maghavān iva
english: That joy of the Kurus, of immeasurable good fortune, was united with her, the daughter of Kuntibhoja, as Maghavan was united with Paulomi.

sanskrit: yātvā devavratenāpi madrāṇāṃ puṭabhedanam viśrutā triṣu lokeṣu mādrī madrapateḥ sutā
english: By Devavrata's going also to the capital of the Madras, Mādrī, daughter of the lord of the Madras, renowned in the three worlds, was obtained.

sanskrit: sarvarājasu vikhyātā rūpeṇāsadṛśī bhuvi pāṇḍor arthe parikrītā dhanena mahatā tadā vivāhaṃ kārayām āsa bhīṣmaḥ pāṇḍor mahātmanaḥ
english: She was celebrated among all kings and unequaled in beauty on earth; she was purchased for Pāṇḍu's sake with great wealth, and then Bhīṣma caused the marriage of the great-souled Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: siṃhoraskaṃ gajaskandham ṛṣabhākṣaṃ manasvinam pāṇḍuṃ dṛṣṭvā naravyāghraṃ vyasmayanta narā bhuvi
english: Seeing Pāṇḍu — lion-chested, elephant-shouldered, bull-eyed, high-minded, that tiger among men — people on earth were filled with wonder.

sanskrit: kṛtodvāhas tataḥ pāṇḍur balotsāhasamanvitaḥ jigīṣamāṇo vasudhāṃ yayau śatrūn anekaśaḥ
english: Then Pāṇḍu, having wed, endowed with strength and enthusiasm, desiring to conquer the earth, went against enemies on many fronts.

sanskrit: pūrvam āgaskṛto gatvā daśārṇāḥ samare jitāḥ pāṇḍunā narasiṃhena kauravāṇāṃ yaśobhṛtā
english: Going first against those who had given offence, the Daśārṇas were conquered in battle by Pāṇḍu, that lion among men, the bearer of the Kauravas' glory.

sanskrit: tataḥ senām upādāya pāṇḍur nānāvidhadhvajām prabhūtahastyaśvarathāṃ padātigaṇasaṃkulām
english: Then Pāṇḍu, taking an army bearing banners of many kinds, rich in elephants, horses, and chariots, and teeming with masses of foot-soldiers —

sanskrit: āgaskṛt sarvavīrāṇāṃ vairī sarvamahībhṛtām goptā magadharāṣṭrasya dārvo rājagṛhe hataḥ
english: — the foe of all heroes, the adversary of all lords of the earth: Darva, the protector of the Magadha realm, was slain at Rājagṛha.

sanskrit: tataḥ kośaṃ samādāya vāhanāni balāni ca pāṇḍunā mithilāṃ gatvā videhāḥ samare jitāḥ
english: Then, after taking treasury, conveyances, and forces, Pāṇḍu marched to Mithilā and conquered the Videhas in battle.

sanskrit: tathā kāśiṣu suhmeṣu puṇḍreṣu bharatarṣabha svabāhubalavīryeṇa kurūṇām akarod yaśaḥ
english: Likewise among the Kāśis, the Suhmas, and the Puṇḍras, O bull of the Bhāratas, by the strength and valor of his own arms he brought glory to the Kurus.

sanskrit: taṃ śaraughamahājvālam astrārciṣam ariṃdamam pāṇḍupāvakam āsādya vyadahyanta narādhipāḥ
english: Coming against him — that tamer of foes blazing like a great fire with showers of arrows and flames of weapons, that Pāṇḍu-conflagration — kings were burned up.

sanskrit: te sasenāḥ sasenena vidhvaṃsitabalā nṛpāḥ pāṇḍunā vaśagāḥ kṛtvā karakarmasu yojitāḥ
english: Those kings, their forces shattered by Pāṇḍu and his forces, were brought into submission and assigned to the works of tribute.

sanskrit: tena te nirjitāḥ sarve pṛthivyāṃ sarvapārthivāḥ tam ekaṃ menire śūraṃ deveṣv iva puraṃdaram
english: By him all those kings of the earth were vanquished; they regarded him alone as the great hero, as the gods regard Purandara.

sanskrit: taṃ kṛtāñjalayaḥ sarve praṇatā vasudhādhipāḥ upājagmur dhanaṃ gṛhya ratnāni vividhāni ca
english: All those lords of the earth came to him with joined palms, bowing low, bearing wealth and various jewels.

sanskrit: maṇimuktāpravālaṃ ca suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ tathā goratnāny aśvaratnāni ratharatnāni kuñjarān
english: Gems, pearls, and coral, gold and silver, choice cattle, choice horses, choice chariots, and elephants —

sanskrit: kharoṣṭramahiṣāṃś caiva yac ca kiṃ cid ajāvikam tat sarvaṃ pratijagrāha rājā nāgapurādhipaḥ
english: — and donkeys, camels, and buffaloes, and whatever sheep and goats there were — all this the king, the lord of Hāstinapura, accepted.

sanskrit: tad ādāya yayau pāṇḍuḥ punar muditavāhanaḥ harṣayiṣyan svarāṣṭrāṇi puraṃ ca gajasāhvayam
english: Taking all that, Pāṇḍu set out again with his army rejoicing, intending to gladden his own kingdom and the city of Hāstinapura.

sanskrit: śaṃtano rājasiṃhasya bharatasya ca dhīmataḥ pranaṣṭaḥ kīrtijaḥ śabdaḥ pāṇḍunā punar uddhṛtaḥ
english: The fame born of glory that had been lost to Shantanu, that lion among kings, and to the wise Bharata, was raised up again by Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: ye purā kururāṣṭrāṇi jahruḥ kurudhanāni ca te nāgapurasiṃhena pāṇḍunā karadāḥ kṛtāḥ
english: Those who had formerly seized the Kuru kingdoms and the wealth of the Kurus were made tribute-paying by Pāṇḍu, the lion of Hāstinapura.

sanskrit: ity abhāṣanta rājāno rājāmātyāś ca saṃgatāḥ pratītamanaso hṛṣṭāḥ paurajānapadaiḥ saha
english: So spoke the assembled kings and their ministers, their minds filled with satisfaction and joy, together with the townspeople and country folk.

sanskrit: pratyudyayus taṃ saṃprāptaṃ sarve bhīṣmapurogamāḥ te nadūram ivādhvānaṃ gatvā nāgapurālayāḥ āvṛtaṃ dadṛśur lokaṃ hṛṣṭā bahuvidhair janaiḥ
english: All went forth to meet him on his arrival, led by Bhīṣma; those dwellers of Hāstinapura, going as if the road were not far, saw joyfully that the whole world was thronged with many kinds of people.

sanskrit: nānāyānasamānītai ratnair uccāvacais tathā hastyaśvaratharatnaiś ca gobhir uṣṭrair athāvikaiḥ nāntaṃ dadṛśur āsādya bhīṣmeṇa saha kauravāḥ
english: With jewels of high and low quality brought on various vehicles, with choice elephants, horses, and chariots, with cattle, camels, and sheep — the Kauravas together with Bhīṣma, coming upon it all, could see no end to it.

sanskrit: so 'bhivādya pituḥ pādau kausalyānandavardhanaḥ yathārhaṃ mānayām āsa paurajānapadān api
english: He, the increaser of Kausalyā's joy, paid reverence to his father's feet, and duly honored the townspeople and country folk as well.

sanskrit: pramṛdya pararāṣṭrāṇi kṛtārthaṃ punarāgatam putram āsādya bhīṣmas tu harṣād aśrūṇy avartayat
english: Bhīṣma, meeting his son who had returned fulfilled in purpose after crushing enemy kingdoms, shed tears of joy.

sanskrit: sa tūryaśatasaṃghānāṃ bherīṇāṃ ca mahāsvanaiḥ harṣayan sarvaśaḥ paurān viveśa gajasāhvayam
english: To the great sounds of hundreds of musical instruments and kettledrums, gladdening the citizens on all sides, he entered Hāstinapura.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca dhṛtarāṣṭrābhyanujñātaḥ svabāhuvijitaṃ dhanam bhīṣmāya satyavatyai ca mātre copajahāra saḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: With Dhṛtarāṣṭra's permission, he presented the wealth conquered by his own arms to Bhīṣma, to Satyavatī, and to his mother.

sanskrit: vidurāya ca vai pāṇḍuḥ preṣayām āsa tad dhanam suhṛdaś cāpi dharmātmā dhanena samatarpayat
english: Pāṇḍu also sent that wealth to Vidura; and that righteous soul fully satisfied his friends with treasure.

sanskrit: tataḥ satyavatīṃ bhīṣmaḥ kausalyāṃ ca yaśasvinīm śubhaiḥ pāṇḍujitai ratnais toṣayām āsa bhārata
english: Then Bhīṣma satisfied Satyavatī and the glorious Kausalyā with auspicious jewels won by Pāṇḍu, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: nananda mātā kausalyā tam apratimatejasam jayantam iva paulomī pariṣvajya nararṣabham
english: His mother Kausalyā rejoiced, embracing that bull among men of matchless splendor, even as Paulomi embraces the victorious Jayanta.

sanskrit: tasya vīrasya vikrāntaiḥ sahasraśatadakṣiṇaiḥ aśvamedhaśatair īje dhṛtarāṣṭro mahāmakhaiḥ
english: With the conquests of that hero, Dhṛtarāṣṭra performed a hundred horse-sacrifices — great rites with hundreds of thousands in sacrificial gifts.

sanskrit: saṃprayuktaś ca kuntyā ca mādryā ca bharatarṣabha jitatandrīs tadā pāṇḍur babhūva vanagocaraḥ
english: Joined together with Kuntī and with Mādrī, O bull of the Bhāratas, Pāṇḍu, free from sloth, then became a wanderer of the forests.

sanskrit: hitvā prāsādanilayaṃ śubhāni śayanāni ca araṇyanityaḥ satataṃ babhūva mṛgayāparaḥ
english: Abandoning his palace dwelling and his fine beds, he became constantly given to forest life, ever devoted to the hunt.

sanskrit: sa caran dakṣiṇaṃ pārśvaṃ ramyaṃ himavato gireḥ uvāsa giripṛṣṭheṣu mahāśālavaneṣu ca
english: Roaming the lovely southern slopes of the Himālayan mountain, he dwelt on mountain ridges and in forests of great shala trees.

sanskrit: rarāja kuntyā mādryā ca pāṇḍuḥ saha vane vasan kareṇvor iva madhyasthaḥ śrīmān pauraṃdaro gajaḥ
english: Pāṇḍu shone in the forest dwelling together with Kuntī and Mādrī, like the splendid elephant of Purandara standing between two she-elephants.

sanskrit: bhārataṃ saha bhāryābhyāṃ bāṇakhaḍgadhanurdharam vicitrakavacaṃ vīraṃ paramāstravidaṃ nṛpam devo 'yam ity amanyanta carantaṃ vanavāsinaḥ
english: The forest dwellers, seeing that Bhārata king roaming with his two wives, bearing arrows, sword, and bow, wearing varied armor, a hero and master of weapons supreme, thought him a god.

sanskrit: tasya kāmāṃś ca bhogāṃś ca narā nityam atandritāḥ upajahrur vanānteṣu dhṛtarāṣṭreṇa coditāḥ
english: Men, ever diligent and urged on by Dhṛtarāṣṭra, brought constantly to the forest his desires and enjoyments.

sanskrit: atha pāraśavīṃ kanyāṃ devakasya mahīpateḥ rūpayauvanasaṃpannāṃ sa śuśrāvāpagāsutaḥ
english: Then the son of the Gaṅgā heard of a Pāraśava maiden, daughter of King Devaka, endowed with beauty and youth.

sanskrit: tatas tu varayitvā tām ānāyya puruṣarṣabhaḥ vivāhaṃ kārayām āsa vidurasya mahāmateḥ
english: Then that bull among men, having wooed and brought her, caused the marriage of the great-minded Vidura.

sanskrit: tasyāṃ cotpādayām āsa viduraḥ kurunandanaḥ putrān vinayasaṃpannān ātmanaḥ sadṛśān guṇaiḥ
english: And Vidura, the joy of the Kurus, begot upon her sons possessed of good breeding, equal to himself in qualities.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ putraśataṃ jajñe gāndhāryāṃ janamejaya dhṛtarāṣṭrasya vaiśyāyām ekaś cāpi śatāt paraḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then, O Janamejaya, a hundred sons were born to Dhṛtarāṣṭra through Gāndhārī, and one more beyond the hundred through a Vaiśya woman.

sanskrit: pāṇḍoḥ kuntyāṃ ca mādryāṃ ca pañca putrā mahārathāḥ devebhyaḥ samapadyanta saṃtānāya kulasya vai
english: To Pāṇḍu through Kuntī and through Mādrī were born five great warriors, obtained from the gods for the continuation of the family line.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca kathaṃ putraśataṃ jajñe gāndhāryāṃ dvijasattama kiyatā caiva kālena teṣām āyuś ca kiṃ param
english: Janamejaya said: How were a hundred sons born to Gāndhārī, O best of twice-born? And in how much time? And what was their highest lifespan?

sanskrit: kathaṃ caikaḥ sa vaiśyāyāṃ dhṛtarāṣṭrasuto 'bhavat kathaṃ ca sadṛśīṃ bhāryāṃ gāndhārīṃ dharmacāriṇīm ānukūlye vartamānāṃ dhṛtarāṣṭro 'tyavartata
english: How did that one son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra come to be through the Vaiśya woman? And how did Dhṛtarāṣṭra transgress against Gāndhārī his wife — a woman of righteous conduct equal to himself, living in devotion to him?

sanskrit: kathaṃ ca śaptasya sataḥ pāṇḍos tena mahātmanā samutpannā daivatebhyaḥ pañca putrā mahārathāḥ
english: And how, from Pāṇḍu who had been cursed by that great soul, were born five sons, great warriors, from the gods?

sanskrit: etad vidvan yathāvṛttaṃ vistareṇa tapodhana kathayasva na me tṛptiḥ kathyamāneṣu bandhuṣu
english: Knowing all this as it happened, tell it in full, O wealth of austerity; I am not satisfied when my kinsmen are being told of.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca kṣucchramābhipariglānaṃ dvaipāyanam upasthitam toṣayām āsa gāndhārī vyāsas tasyai varaṃ dadau
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Gāndhārī satisfied Dvaipāyana when he came, worn out by hunger and fatigue; and Vyāsa gave her a boon.

sanskrit: sā vavre sadṛśaṃ bhartuḥ putrāṇāṃ śatam ātmanaḥ tataḥ kālena sā garbhaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭrād athāgrahīt
english: She chose a hundred sons equal to her husband and herself; then in time she conceived through Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: saṃvatsaradvayaṃ taṃ tu gāndhārī garbham āhitam aprajā dhārayām āsa tatas tāṃ duḥkham āviśat
english: Gāndhārī, childless, bore that planted embryo for two full years; then sorrow overtook her.

sanskrit: śrutvā kuntīsutaṃ jātaṃ bālārkasamatejasam udarasyātmanaḥ sthairyam upalabhyānvacintayat
english: Hearing that a son of Kuntī had been born, blazing in splendor like the morning sun, she reflected upon the steadfastness of her own womb.
